decision: Add Arrow and Avnet (SEC XBRL: revenue, COGS, inventory, receivables) as the Nordic-side distributor tier
reason: Arrow and Avnet are Nordic's franchised distributors; Ingram / TD Synnex sit on the Logitech side and peripherals are 1-2% of their sales, so their inventory says nothing about Nordic parts
evidence: Pipeline C config/distributors.csv (authorized list); Nordic AR2025 IFRS 8.34 (two distributors = 30% + 12% of revenue)
effect: comp_dist_dio_avg, arrow_dio, avnet_dio in factors_quarterly.csv; Nordic channel call

decision: Use Microchip's 10-Q/10-K sentence 'our distributors maintained NN days of inventory' as the numeric MCU-channel series (2020Q2-2026Q2)
alternatives_considered: Silicon Labs (closest BLE peer); keep channel only as a coded state
reason: It is the only recurring numeric distribution-inventory disclosure in an audited/reviewed filing we found. Silicon Labs was checked and discloses only its OWN days of inventory, so the earlier claim that it gives channel weeks was wrong and is withdrawn
evidence: SEC full-text search + the filings (mchp_distributor_days.csv carries the verbatim quote; 21/21 chain checks pass)
effect: mchp_disti_days factor; distributor-cover prior; Nordic channel call percentile

decision: Logitech: quarterly raw materials / finished goods from XBRL. Nordic: year-end raw materials (wafers) / WIP / finished goods from the annual-report note
reason: Nordic does not split inventory in quarterly reports; an estimate would be a number without evidence. The 2026 build (USD 155m -> 217m) therefore has no stage split until AR2026 - a stated blind spot and a question for the 22 Oct call
evidence: AR2021-AR2025 notes; sums equal reported inventory (max 0.08%); prior-year columns chain
effect: nordic_inventory_stage.csv; Bernard-Noel stage spreads; Nordic call question

decision: Do not compute GN DIO / DSO / stage factors; GN enters step 3 only through the Enterprise sell-out minus sell-in gap
reason: GN's group balance sheet mixes Hearing (~45% of revenue, sold to Amplifon end-2026, reclassified held-for-sale in 2026: inventory 2,314 -> 1,551 DKKm in one quarter). A group ratio would measure the divestment, not the Enterprise channel
effect: GN channel index only; GN call graded D

decision: Exact flow recursion F_t = F_{t-4}(1+g_out) - gap_t x S_{t-4}
reason: The naive reading assumes the year-ago quarter was balanced; after a drain it books the lapping as a build (2024Q1: naive +48m, exact -14m). Logitech's CFO made the same point: '2 points of that is simply comparing the channel inventory year-over-year'
effect: channel_index_logitech.csv, channel_index_gn.csv

decision: A quarter with no disclosed gap (after the series starts) is treated as gap = 0
reason: Logitech and GN quantify the gap when it is material; silence is weak evidence of 'about zero'. Interpolation would invent a number
effect: GN 2024Q4 and 2025Q4 set to 0 (flagged grade D)

decision: Pin the level so the five quarters in which Logitech management said the channel was at target average zero; report the anchor spread (rms) as the index's error bar, and a latest-anchor variant
alternatives_considered: Assume the first quarter is balanced
reason: The recursion gives changes, not levels. Management's own 'at target' statements are the only public level information; their mutual disagreement is an honest error bar
evidence: config/anchors.csv (quotes checked against data/manual excerpts at run time)
effect: 2026Q2 reading -2.1 wk (all anchors) / -1.1 wk (latest anchor); rms 0.73 wk

decision: Primary start = the start (2021Q2 or 2023Q1) whose anchor readings agree better (smaller rms); the other is reported
alternatives_considered: Always start at the first grade-C quarter
reason: 2021Q2-2022Q4 gaps are grade D (uncited); letting management's anchors arbitrate is a rule stated before seeing which start wins
effect: 2023Q1 chosen (0.73 vs 0.82 wk); readings differ by <0.3 wk

decision: Do not apply the whole-company amplitude (2.5x destock / 5.5x recovery) to the Logitech or GN slice of Nordic revenue. Logitech slice: 0.27 / 1.0 / 1.24x its own sell-in; GN slice: 1.0 / 2.5 / 3.9x
alternatives_considered: Use the whole-company multiplier for every slice
reason: Nordic's Q4 2023 report: top-10 Bluetooth customers -3% in 2023 vs broad market -46%. Logitech is a top-10 customer on step 2's p10 estimate (USD 62m/yr vs top-10 average 27.6m). GN (p50 USD 9m) may be broad market -> wide range
evidence: nordic_customer_concentration.csv (7 quotes verified in the cached reports); slice_multiplier.csv
effect: model.yaml regime amplitude_multiplier relabelled as whole-company; no code read it, so no forecast changes

decision: State the cover at every stocking point before fitting: measured from filings where possible (Logitech DIO / FG weeks, Microchip distributor days x distribution share), assumptions where not (retail channel 4-8 wk, ODM stock 2-8 wk)
reason: Judgment checklist item 1: the data validate or reject a stated prior
effect: total prior 14-31 weeks end demand -> Nordic

decision: Reduced form kept = demand elasticity only (y = a + b g_{t-L}). The accelerator term c(g - g_{t-4}) and the stock-gap term gamma x (distributor days - normal) are estimated and reported, not kept
alternatives_considered: Keep the full structural equation; keep the one-quarter accelerator dg
reason: Accelerator: c = 0.00 +/- 0.04 at the Logitech channel and ~0 at Logitech's own stock (both same-quarter, well identified); at Nordic its sign flips with the lag (-29 / -4 / +24 weeks for lags 1/2/3) = not identified. Stock gap: |t| < 1 and leave-one-out error rises. Inventory information therefore enters as STATE in the channel call, not as a coefficient
evidence: mechanism_tests.csv; chain_consistency.csv (product of the three link elasticities 1.97 vs direct 1.90)
effect: Nordic demand elasticity b = 1.90 (90% bootstrap 1.2-3.4, lag 2) used as the cross-check; step 6 ridge regression unchanged

decision: Driver = Logitech sell-through YoY = total net sales YoY + disclosed gap
reason: The gap is disclosed for the total company; adding a company-level gap to a category-level sell-in would mix bases. Step 6 keeps the radio-category driver; the two are compared in the report
effect: logi_sellthrough_yoy column

decision: Nordic-tier regressions use 2022Q3-2026Q2; the supply-constrained regime (2020Q3-2022Q2) is excluded
alternatives_considered: Full sample with a regime dummy
reason: In 2021-22 Nordic revenue was set by wafer supply (backlog > USD 1bn), not by orders: the ordering rule does not apply. A dummy would spend one of 16 degrees of freedom to average over it

decision: Variance ratio of YoY growth per link and regime, with a moving-block bootstrap 90% interval; normal-regime ratios flagged as ill-conditioned
reason: The variance ratio is the literature's measure (Lee et al. 1997; Cachon et al. 2007); YoY removes seasonality. In a calm window the denominator hardly moves, so the ratio explodes (link B normal: 49x) - the same artefact behind the '5.5x recovery'
effect: '5.5x in the recovery' reclassified as a small-denominator artefact plus Nordic share / content gains (trend a ~ 9-14 pts/yr)

decision: Step 3's channel adjustments are cross-checks printed next to the forecast lines they correspond to; they do not overwrite config/model.yaml
alternatives_considered: Let step 3 set the forecast adjustments
reason: config/model.yaml is the single place for assumptions (CLAUDE.md). Where step 3 disagrees the report says so and the analyst decides
effect: Logitech: step 3 mid is above the config line (flagged); Nordic and GN inside

decision: No YoY DSO comparison across 2024Q4
reason: Nordic: receivables fell to USD 66m at end-2024 'reflecting improved collection' - a policy change, not a demand signal
effect: nordic_dso_yoy_chg from 2025Q4

decision: Forward DIO on the NEXT quarter's guidance (Nordic: revenue guide x trailing margin because the GM guide is a floor); an ex-post version is labelled diagnostic
reason: Realised COGS is not known at the balance-sheet date - using it is look-ahead
effect: nordic_fwd_dio, logi_fwd_dio

decision: Read Nordic's 2024 'top-10 Bluetooth customers accounted for 58% of revenue' as a share of Bluetooth revenue
reason: The 2023 figure (57%) reconciles only to Bluetooth revenue (276/484); consistency. Graded C because the 2024 sentence is ambiguous
effect: 2024 top-10 / broad split

decision: YoY growth everywhere; the accelerator is derived for a target on trailing-twelve-month demand
reason: With Logitech's Q4 -> Q1 drop (~25%) the one-quarter version does not cancel seasonality (the term is g_t - r g_{t-1} with r the seasonal ratio); the TTM target is also how planners set weeks-of-cover
effect: c x 52 = cover in weeks

decision: No Amazon sell-out scrape, no weekly Digi-Key/Mouser tracker, no Avnet book-to-bill series, no GN DSO
reason: Each costs more than its information: Amazon BSR is a rank not units; distributor stock snapshots exist in Pipeline C already; book-to-bill is verbal; GN group balance sheet is contaminated (D4). The highest-uncertainty node is the channel LEVEL, which none of these would fix
effect: stated limits in the README

decision: Logitech deficit range: low = latest-anchor reading (-1.1 wk), mid = mean of latest-anchor and all-anchor readings, high = the most negative reading
alternatives_considered: Median of the three readings; all-anchor reading only
reason: The five 'at target' anchors drift from +1.2 to -1.0 wk over 2025Q1-2026Q1 while management kept saying 'at target': either Logitech is lowering its weeks-on-hand target or the coded gaps run ~0.5 pt/quarter high. Both argue for the latest anchor as the least-biased level; the all-anchor and alternative-start readings are nearly the same calculation, so a median would double-count them
effect: Logitech refill mid falls from ~48 to ~37 USDm

topic: cycle state from the mechanism data (step 3b)
decision: Classify every quarter's channel-cycle phase (building / drawdown / lean / normal) from Microchip's distributor days (2007-2026), point in time (expanding median / IQR); measure what each phase means as the 12 peers' and Nordic's guidance miss grouped by the phase of t-1 (known at the forecast date: Microchip's 10-Q for t-1 comes after most guides for t, before the actual), errors clustered by quarter; report the transition matrix and the latest phase. Rule in config cycle_state
alternatives_considered: Keep hand-set regime windows; Hamilton Markov-switching on the same series (more parameters on 75 quarters, same reading); use Nordic's own misses only (21 quarters)
reason: Analyst request 2026-09-27: the regime was typed in, not read from data; the cycle is the mechanism question's own output (distributor inventory). Rule revised once after seeing the first classification and the beats by state: a fall in days counts as drawdown only from an above-normal level (only excess can be worked down); a fall from a low level is tightening (2020Q4-2021Q3 shortage) and counts as lean. Disclosed as a researcher degree of freedom
effect: Data dates building 2022Q4-2024Q2 (hand-set destock 2022Q3-2024Q1), drawdown 2024Q4-2025Q2 (hand-set 'normal'), lean 2020Q4-2022Q3 and 2026Q1-Q2. Peers beat 1.28 pts less in building than in other phases (t -3.2, 621 firm-quarters, 64 quarters; with the phase of t-2, known when the guide was set: -1.69, t -4.5); Nordic -3.2% in building (n 7). Latest (2026Q2) lean; next quarter building with p 0.06. Forecast not changed (cross-check)

topic: disclosure table (who holds, who bears, who discloses)
decision: One table per tier and company: holder, the inventory risk it bears, what it discloses about its own and its channel's inventory (numeric / verbal / nothing), what stays hidden, and the model series that stand in for it
reason: The brief asks how each company discloses or hides inventory; the facts were spread over step 3's report, the metric catalogue and data_config

topic: supply shortage split from a lean channel (Nordic)
decision: A quarter the industry state reads 'lean' is a SHORTAGE for Nordic when its own supply data show unmet demand: order backlog above two quarters of revenue (disclosed 2020Q4-2023Q1) or an authorized-distributor lead time above 26 weeks (live, findchips). Column state_nordic in cycle_state.csv; the industry state (peers, Logitech, gamma) stays four-way
alternatives_considered: (a) chip makers' own inventory as the second signal (stated first: lean AND peer-median own DIO below its point-in-time median); (b) Nordic's own inventory days; (c) a hand-dated shortage window; (d) no split
reason: Distributor days alone cannot tell 'wanted but could not get' from 'did not want' - both read lean, so the 2020Q4-2022Q3 shortage and the 2025-26 post-destock caution were one state. (a) flags no quarter, not even 2021: industry own inventory stayed above its median (WIP piles up while finished goods run short; the level rose for 15 years). (b) separates the two episodes (57-94 days vs 141-193) but starts in 2021Q1, so it cannot be read point in time for the shortage. (c) contradicts the data-dated state (D22). Backlog and lead time are the direct measures of unmet demand; the thresholds follow from normal lead times (12-16 weeks ~ one quarter of backlog), not from the data
evidence: backlog / quarterly revenue: 2019Q4 ~1.3 (derived), 2020Q4 3.9, 2021Q4 9.9, 2022Q3 5.4, 2023Q1 4.2; live lead time 16 weeks (2026-09-22); peer-median own DIO 2021: 112-120 days vs point-in-time median 108
effect: 2020Q4-2022Q3 -> shortage for Nordic; 2026Q2 stays lean. Used by F30 in step 7. Analyst decision 2026-09-27

topic: Nordic's own channel: size from its top-10 vs broad market, direction from its own words
decision: Nordic's channel is read from Nordic's own disclosures, not from the Microchip proxy: yearly size = (broad-market growth - top-10 growth) x last year's broad-market revenue (top-10 customers, served mostly direct, stand in for sell-through; the broad market is mostly distribution); quarterly direction = Nordic's coded wording about its distributors' stock. Microchip's distributor days stay the state signal (their turns match Nordic's words within one quarter) and are never used as Nordic's channel level
alternatives_considered: Microchip days as Nordic's channel level (rejected: opposite phase, P128); a quarterly dollar regression of revenue on end demand calibrated on quarters Nordic calls normal (rejected: 5 such quarters); a Kalman filter with a latent channel stock (not built: 22 quarters and ordinal wording, the prior would drive it)
reason: The brief asks where inventory sits and who discloses it; Nordic discloses its channel only in words and in the annual top-10 / broad-market split, so those are its own channel data
evidence: outputs nordic_channel_size.csv (2022 -43.5m, 2023 -164.0m, 2024 -7.7m: -215m, ~29 weeks of 2022 broad-market sales; Arrow / Avnet all-vendor cover 7.0 / 9.0 weeks at 2021Q4, 9.9 / 14.5 at 2023Q4); nordic_wording_vs_microchip_shifts.csv (levels correlate -0.17 to -0.86 at shifts -3..+4)
effect: No forecast number changes. The drained stock cannot all have sat at distributors, so the destock buffer was largely small customers' component stock (Nordic Q2 2024: end customers still excessive into 2025), a node the supply graph lacks; E01 (4/6/8 weeks, capped by distributor cover) describes the normal channel only

topic: State table reads Nordic's guide errors from the raw series, not the panel

reason: one record, two readers: the state table and the habit model must count the same quarters (F32)
evidence: tests/test_cycle_state.py; outputs beat_by_cycle_state.csv sample 'nordic' n = number of guided quarters
